details.catalog: The AI assistant vendor's catalog (for example ChatGPT's app directory). {{castBrand}} submits its connector once; the vendor reviews and lists it; members add it from the catalog at no cost. The catalog never holds member credentials: sign-in and consent still happen at {{castBrand}}'s own identity provider on first use.
details.member: A {{castProgram}} member. Authenticates {{castBrand}} from the agent, but {{castBrand}} never sees the member credentials and the agent never sees the member session.
details.agent: Whatever the member brought: ChatGPT in a browser, a mobile assistant, a coding CLI. {{castBrand}} controls none of it and trusts none of it. It holds no standing credential; it mints a token per call.
details.door: The only internet-facing hop. PingGateway MCP module: validates aud and scope, tool allowlist, audit per call. No direct agent-to-resource path exists on the network.
details.pingone: PingOne: sign-in with passkey or MFA, consent through the Agreement step, CIMD or direct-API client registration, and RFC 8693 token exchange. Issues bearer tokens only (no DPoP, no mTLS binding).
details.authorize: PingOne Authorize evaluates member, agent, tool and amount. PingOne Protect scores the session for agentic automation. Verdicts: permit, deny, step-up.
details.app: {{castBrand}}'s own surface, in {{castBrand}}'s branding. One approval, one action; the approval receipt is single use. The human approves a transaction, never a session.
details.rewards: Accepts only its own audience. Behind it the Facade is the only component holding the legacy credentials; the web session lives in Redis keyed by a hash of the Ping token and is never returned to the client.
details.audit: Gateway and authorization server write sub, act.client_id, jti and the verdict. Disabling the agent's client registration revokes its access within one token lifetime; the member's own session is unaffected.
